newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cabinet reshuffle stuck in party talks.
newsitem.headline: Czech cabinet reshuffle stuck in party talks.

text.p: A first round of talks between Czech coalition parties on a cabinet reshuffle ended inconclusively on Monday, two days after the finance and interior ministers resigned.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, who leads the senior Civic Democratic Party (ODS), began discussing the extent of the shake-up with coalition partners after the two ministers, both from the ODS, stepped down on Saturday.

The leaders agreed to change the cabinet last week in order to answer a sharp drop in the centre-right government's approval ratings amid an economic downturn and a widespread feeling that financial crime is pervasive.

But Monday's meeting suggested agreement on the share-out of ministerial posts reshuffle would be difficult. "We clearly indicated our mutual limits and the corridor within which we can move," Klaus told journalists afterwards.
"The only outcome (of Monday's talks) I can say is that the corridor which exists after today, if it was played to the finish line in this way, has a solution."
He declined to elaborate, and party leaders set another meeting for noon on Tuesday.
The coalition talks look to be snagged on the issue of finding room for the leader of the junior Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), Michael Zantovsky, in the 16-member cabinet.
Zantovsky, who took over as ODA chairman in March after serving as ambassador to Washington, was directed by his party leadership on Saturday to take a seat in the government.

But the former psychologist and journalist Zantovsky is widely believed to be most interested in either the foreign ministry or defence portfolios, both of which are held by the other coalition parties.

Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux, who heads the junior Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), has been cool to giving up the defence portfolio, while ODS is not expected to be willing to part with the foreign ministry post.
The ODA has the justice, environment, and industry and trade portfolios as well as the minister without portfolio.
Lux hinted that the Monday talks only sought to set ground rules for more negotiations.

"I welcomed the ability to agree on certain formalisation of coalition negotiations, above all with the aim to find a way of consensual action on some declared issues," Lux told the joint news conference alongside Klaus and Zantovsky.
The party leaders all shunned President Vaclav Havel's suggestion over the weekend that the whole government's resignation would be a cleaner, if less practical, solution.
"If we didn't agree (on changes)... of course, we could not be a coalition any longer," Klaus said on Monday.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Interior Minister Jan Ruml announced their resignations at a meeting on Saturday of ODS leaders.

Klaus's chief adviser Jiri Weigl, who helped formulate much of the government's economic programme but is not affiliated with a political party, was nominated by the ODS to replace Kocarnik at the finance ministry..
As widely expected, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy of the junior Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), told his party on Saturday he would also resign.
The cabinet shuffle has become even more sensitive as pressure mounts on the Czech crown, which has been hit by foreign speculators reacting to poor macroeconomic results and political instability.
